headline: President Clinton created a board to look into a labor dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and some of its union workers.
what_it_does: This order set up an emergency board to study a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain employees represented by the United Transportation Union. Under federal railroad labor law, such boards usually look into the facts and suggest a way to settle the dispute. Creating a board also generally delays strikes or lockouts for a set period while it does its work.

who_it_affects.group: Long Island Rail Road employees represented by the United Transportation Union
who_it_affects.how: Their dispute with the railroad went to an emergency board for review, which typically delays any strike for a time.
The railroad's dispute with these workers was placed before a federal board for investigation and recommendations.
Creating the board likely put off a possible work stoppage that could have disrupted train service.
